revisions.reason: Every creature gained an authored class, danger tier and feeding role, and the file gained a roles section holding the biome range map each role shares. `size` had been acting as a de-facto tier in lock-step with spacing and occurrence, which is why a gray wolf and a European rabbit carried identical placement rules.

Profile document version 2: 32 monsters re-tiered against the tier definitions (drakes are not dragons, fodder undead can hurt rather than kill, liches and the great sea monsters are campaign threats) and 257 species added, 141 monsters and 116 animals weighted to the harmless end, so the catalogue is a pyramid like the placement budget it is divided into. Every monster family now spans all five tiers. Placement moves for every seed because the tier budget is shared among whoever qualifies.

User-authorized hidden bestiary: the blood and void nest families and the eldritch-gated aberrants. Every entry requires a hidden school's potency, which is zero in any generated world, so none can be placed by generation.

Creature movement classes: every profile declares `movement` (nester | migratory | irruptive | follower | drifter), defaulting to nester so no existing creature changes behaviour, and seventeen creatures are added that only exist because movement does -- wandering dead with no grave to return to, irruptive swarms out of marginal ground, followers that derive their route from a host, migratory herds, and a barrow wight added deliberately as the stationary contrast. The undead split follows a rule rather than a tag: an undead with a grave nests at it, an undead without one wanders. Profiles 663 -> 680. Behavior reviewed is the movement field and the added rows; coverage is Sim/tests/test_creature_movement.py, which asserts structural placeability rather than observed placement. Documented in docs/nomads.md.

revisions.reason: Documentation only. An attempt to replace sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b)) with explicit addition was reverted: CPython 3.12 sums floats with Neumaier compensation, so the explicit form differs by about one ULP and silently changes generated worlds on some seeds. The comment records why this sum() must stay.

Habitat placement split into two independent passes, animals then monsters, each a thinned point process over the ground rather than a lottery under a fixed anchor cap. Tier carries the ecology: density falls geometrically with danger, and the pyramid is a per-medium world budget so a tier cannot forfeit its share by being habitat-specialised. Settlement clearance is folded into the intensity instead of rejecting a draw after it. Counts now scale with habitable area, which the 120 cap prevented.

The city ceiling is the ground's own packing limit rather than a constant 24, so a larger world supports more cities instead of the same two dozen.

Asking for no cities outranks the systemic ceiling. Making the ceiling the ground's packing had let settlement_count zero mean "no ceiling" rather than "no cities", and the diaspora bonus -- which exists to waive a zero quota -- then settled worlds that two tests require to stay empty.

Age-transition wars: contested neighbours fight over ground and road-linked supply, named civil, regional or international by the relationship between the participants. The loser becomes a ruin that names the war and may leave a leyline key point where a school already held its ground; both sides record the war, survivors carry it across the rebuild, and a veteran city raises the fortress demand, its own ceiling and its regional threat. Settlement schema 15, history 2, rural report 8, threat assessment 2.

Bound the city packing ceiling by raster resolution as well as habitable area. Spacing alone bounded density while the world was 11 km across and a cell was 87 m; on a 200 km world a size-17 grid has 12.5 km cells against an 8 km spacing, so the area ceiling admitted about 63 cities onto 289 nodes, each planning a full crop. The binding spacing is now whichever of the two is coarser, which changes nothing at rasters fine enough for the spacing to dominate.

Honour an explicitly lowered settlement_count even on the inferred path. The parameter is published as "Maximum surface cities" but the inferred branch discarded it, so a request for two cities returned ten; the recipe default still means "no ceiling but the ground".

Name settlements from each people's own language instead of a 24-word English list indexed by founding order. The index was the defect: names[k%24] renamed every later city when one was founded earlier, and could not survive an age advance without the downstream copy-back. Naming now keys on the node and its coordinates, runs in node order so collision redraws are canonical, and returns a gloss beside each name. The native mirror in Core/scene.cpp still holds the old list and is deferred to the native port phase, so city names differ between the reference and the port until then.

Beast nest options restated for the two passes: per-medium densities and tier falloffs replace the single density, and the anchor ceilings default to zero, meaning the ground decides. Also adds the orogeny bound.

Route defence is read from the world instead of a constant: road length / support reach plus distinct river crossings, ceilinged by the city count, with fortress_count demoted to a caller's maximum whose default no longer binds. Retires the static four fortresses every world size used to get; rural report 7 and its fortress_demand record, with age advancement refusing older reports.
User-requested lunar cycle: add the lunar_influence world option (default .5) that scales how far lunar surges sway the age lottery. Astrology contract documented in docs/astrology.md.

Authored world shape: circumference_km and relief_m registry entries consumed by the request builder to derive globe_radius, tectonic_relief, amplitude, wavelength and orogeny (including the wavelength Core/genesis.cpp world_shape_overrides never derives, without which a world past ~150 km resolves no surface noise). world_size presets move from 11/22/33 km to 200/400/600 km circumference. Grid ceiling raised 257 to 1025.

Derive settlement_spacing, support_reach and culture_link_cost from circumference in the request builder. derive_population would have scaled them but is unreachable on recipe 3 (auto_parameters is forbidden there), so a 200 km world kept the 450 m / 1000 m reference defaults: 222 cities, a support reach of a sixth of one cell, and zero hamlets and zero fortresses.
User-requested moon controls: moon_variation and explicit moon cycle/tilt options (zero means seeded) so the lunar cycle is controllable from the generation API. Documented in docs/astrology.md.
World option `war_survival` (default 0, identity preserved): the chance a defeated city survives a war as a vassal. Documented in docs/terrain-world-layers.md.

User-authorized twelve-school taxonomy: declare the four hidden schools as options so generate_networks can read them, with occurrence locked at min == max == 0 so no request can raise one during generation.
User-authorized super villains: villain_rise, villain_hold and villain_density, all defaulting to a world that raises none, so an untouched world carries no villains block at all.

User-authorized corruption API: hidden schools saturate above the known eight (strength 1.15). At equal strength a corrupted cell cannot clear dominant_school's 0.08 margin over a strong radiant or earth field, so corrupted ground would never mutate and corruption would be invisible.

Nomads: four registry options -- nomad_occurrence, nomad_density (bands per thousand square kilometres of habitable land, so the count follows the ground rather than the raster), nomad_variation for independent reroll, and beast_movement_share to thin the travelling creature groups. No per-classification multipliers: the six gates already decide what a start point can raise, and a knob nothing reads is worse than no knob. Behavior reviewed is the option declarations; coverage is Sim/tests/test_terrain_nomads.py and docs/nomads.md.

Raise the age-advance grid ceiling from 257 to 1025 so a world can hold both its history and its full terrain. The octave admission filter needs step <= wavelength/2, which at this planet's 14,702 m wavelength first admits the fifth of five noise octaves at size 513 -- above the old age-advance refusal, so until now a world could have all of its terrain or all of its history and never both. No generated bytes change: this widens which inputs are accepted, not what any accepted input produces. Core/genesis.hpp max_grid moves in the same change so the reference and the port agree on the accepted range.

Restate octave admission without a per-planet metre figure. wavelength/step reduces to 1.6*(n-1)/(2*pi*sqrt(plate_count)), so the globe radius cancels and the crossover depends on grid size and plate count alone; the previous comment quoted 14,702 m, which is one planet's wavelength and sends a reader on any other radius to crossovers this generator will never produce. Also records that 1025 admits no octave beyond 513. Comment only; no behavior, contract or generated byte changes.
